indicators.flag: Disabling or Manipulating the Automatic Identification System (AIS) on Vessels
indicators.red_flag: AIS transponder disabled or its transmitted data manipulated to mask vessel movement
indicators.rationale: AIS disablement/spoofing is vessel-navigation behavior on the high seas that a financial institution cannot observe from its transaction or payment data; closing this requires an external maritime AIS-tracking feed.

indicators.red_flag: Vessel name or IMO number physically painted over or altered to obscure its identity
indicators.rationale: Painting over a hull name or IMO number is a physical-vessel tampering signal with no footprint in FI transaction data; detection needs port-state inspection or vessel-imagery sources.

indicators.red_flag: Falsified cargo and vessel shipping documents
indicators.rationale: A trade-finance bank does handle bills of lading, invoices, and certificates of origin, but verifying their authenticity (disguised petroleum/metals origin) requires enriching transaction records with external trade-document and origin-validation data the FI does not natively hold.

indicators.flag:
Ship-to-Ship (STS) Transfers
While ship-to-ship transfers (the transfer of cargo between ships at sea) can be conducted for
legitimate purposes, STS transfers—especially at night or in areas determined to be high-risk for
sanctions evasion or other illicit activity—are frequently used to evade sanctions by concealing the
origin or destination of surreptitiously transferred petroleum, coal, and other material.
indicators.red_flag: Ship-to-ship cargo transfers at sea, especially at night or in high-risk areas, concealing the origin or destination of the transferred goods
indicators.rationale: Cargo transferred between ships at sea (often at night in high-risk areas) is invisible to an FI's payment ledger; surfacing it requires maritime AIS/dark-activity tracking feeds.

indicators.flag:
Voyage Irregularities
Malign actors may attempt to disguise the ultimate destination or origin of cargo or recipients by
using indirect routing, unscheduled detours, or transit or transshipment of cargo through third
countries.
indicators.red_flag: Indirect routing, unscheduled detours, or third-country transshipment disguising the origin or destination of cargo
indicators.rationale: Indirect routing and third-country transshipment leave a partial trace in trade-payment counterparties and shipping terms, but distinguishing it from legitimate transshipment requires enriching the transaction with external routing/port-call data.

indicators.red_flag: Vessel flag falsified, or the vessel repeatedly re-registered with new flag states to avoid detection
indicators.rationale: Vessel flag-state registration and deregistration history lives in flag-registry data, not FI transaction data; detecting flag hopping requires an external vessel-registry feed.

indicators.red_flag: Shell companies or multiple layers of ownership and management used to disguise the ultimate beneficial owner
indicators.rationale: Shell-company layering and frequent ownership/management changes to obscure the ultimate beneficial owner is the one practice an FI can observe from its own KYC and counterparty data — a classic AML beneficial-ownership-obfuscation pattern over the customer's existing payment and ownership records.

build_logic.logic: Flag a maritime/commodity-trade counterparty when the beneficial-ownership chain cannot be resolved within a threshold depth AND the structure shows shell-company indicators (no operating footprint, address-sharing) OR a pattern of ownership/ISM-management changes exceeding a baseline within a rolling window.
build_logic.window: rolling 180 days for ownership/management-change counting; point-in-time UBO resolution at onboarding and periodic refresh
build_logic.source: KYC/onboarding beneficial-ownership records, corporate-registry counterparty data, payment counterparty ledger
build_logic.route: enhanced due diligence / sanctions-evasion review queue
